chunks: And he, peace be upon him and his family, said:

"Allah, Blessed and Exalted, said: 'Fasting is for Me, and I reward for it.' And the fasting person has two joys: when he breaks his fast and when he meets his Lord, Mighty and Majestic. By the One in whose hand is the soul of Muhammad, the breath of the fasting person is more fragrant with Allah than the scent of musk."

key_terms.أَجْزِي: I reward; Allah's direct recompense for the act of fasting
key_terms.الصَّوْمُ: sawm (fasting), the act of worship uniquely attributed to Allah in this hadith
key_terms.خُلُوفُ: the changed odor of the mouth caused by fasting
key_terms.رِيحِ الْمِسْكِ: the scent of musk; used as a comparison for fragrance
key_terms.فَرْحَتَانِ: two joys; the two moments of happiness promised to the fasting person
key_terms.لِلصَّائِمِ: for the fasting person; the one observing the fast
key_terms.يَلْقَى: he meets; referring to meeting his Lord
key_terms.يُفْطِرُ: he breaks his fast; the time of ending the daily fast

ai.seo_question: What does the hadith mean when Allah says, 'Fasting is for Me, and I reward for it'?
ai.summary: This hadith states the special station of sawm (fasting) before Allah, who ascribes it to Himself and promises its reward. It also describes the believer's immediate joy at iftar and ultimate joy in meeting his Lord, while honoring even the altered breath of the fasting person as beloved to Allah.
